chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-mut'ah, is it one of the four? He said: No.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْأَرْبَع: The four (referring to a specific set of conditions or types mentioned in the context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mut'ah according to this hadith from al-Ishtibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies a specific legal nuance regarding *Mut'ah* (temporary marriage), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) negates its inclusion in a previously discussed category of 'the four,' likely referring to the four types of divorce or specific marital conditions debated in juristic circles. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly tradition's precision in categorizing *Mut'ah* as a distinct, independent form of marriage rather than a subset of permanent marital arrangements. The narration underscores the importance of contextual interpretation in fiqh, ensuring that *Mut'ah* is not conflated with other marital structures.
